title: When to quit your job as a solopreneur: Alex West's 10 reasons and the asymmetric-risk test
summary: Alex West explains why he quit his job after Cyberleads out-earned his salary for six months, and distills a decision framework. Quit when results are consistent, you've stopped learning, you have 2+ years of runway, and the downside is capped while the upside is life-changing.

principles.text: Quit only after your business has consistently beaten your salary, not after one lucky spike.
principles.quote: my my business had made more than my salary for 6 months in a row

principles.text: Take asymmetric risks: cheap, playful bets where the downside is small and the upside is large; be conservative on ruinous ones.
principles.quote: with other risk it should be the opposite right like you should be wild you should be experimental and you should be very playful and those are risks that they won't ruin you if they go wrong

principles.text: Stack the odds before leaving: save runway while employed so a total failure still leaves years to recover.
principles.quote: I managed to set aside 50k which means that even if for some reason I was to start making 0 per month starting from tomorrow

principles.text: Embrace the wild, viral nature of social media as a channel instead of trying to make it predictable.
principles.quote: embrace the unpredictable viral nature of social media and go with it

principles.text: For software businesses, a calm mind and one correct scaled decision beat long hours; two focused hours can drive most results.
principles.quote: taking a simple correct decision and scaling it is far more important than the number of hours you put in

principles.text: Small companies' scale is an illusion: a 50-person company is really a handful of doers plus people just moving tasks along, so incumbents are beatable.
principles.quote: when you're competing with a 50% PE uh company you're essentially competing against five people and 45 Yes Men
